1.name: Keyboard Tab traversal surfaces visible focus on interactive elements
1.root_cause_hypothesis: The most likely hosting-side issue is that the production bundle being served either lacks a visibly distinct keyboard-focus style or has that style overridden/hidden by other CSS loaded in the hosted environment. Common causes include a global reset that removes outlines, a component/theme stylesheet with equal-or-higher specificity that makes focus visuals blend into hover/active states, or a deployment/cache mismatch where the live site is serving an older build with incomplete focus styles. As a result, Tab navigation moves focus, but the outline is too subtle or indistinguishable to confirm in screenshots.
1.error_message:
Result: Visible keyboard focus outlines on Tab navigation could not be reliably confirmed.

Summary of observations (directly from this session):
- The homepage was loaded and contains approximately 27 interactive elements.
- Multiple attempts were made to verify keyboard focus outlines:
  - Tab keypresses were sent repeatedly (multiple steps, ~4 distinct Tab sequences and ~8 similar actions overall).
  - Clicks were used to set focus before tabbing on these elements: brand link (index 7974, "Matchday Forecast"), Home (index 7984), and theme-toggle button (index 7912).
- A page search located focus-related CSS keywords: 'focus-visible', ':focus', and 'outline', indicating the stylesheet references focus styles.
- Despite these attempts, the screenshots taken after actions do not show an unambiguous, high-contrast keyboard focus outline on the focused elements. Some header items have green rounded styling, but that styling cannot be reliably attributed to keyboard focus (could be hover/active styling) from the captured images.

Conclusion: The requirement — that pressing Tab repeatedly advances focus and each newly focused element displays a visible focus outline — could not be verified. Either the site does not apply sufficiently visible focus outlines for keyboard navigation, or the focus styles are visually indistinguishable in screenshots. Because the visible focus outline could not be confirmed after multiple controlled attempts, the test is marked as not successful.

Recommendation: To make the behavior testable and accessible, ensure focus styles are visible and high contrast (for example, apply a distinct outline or box-shadow on :focus and :focus-visible that differs from hover/active visuals). After such a change, re-run the keyboard navigation test and verify the focus outline is clearly visible in screenshots.
1.recommended_fix_target: Update the deployed frontend styling so keyboard focus is unmistakable on interactive elements: define a strong :focus-visible state with a high-contrast outline/box-shadow and sufficient offset, and ensure it is not removed or overridden by global CSS resets, component libraries, or theme styles. If a CSS-in-JS or build step is used, verify the focus styles are included in production and not purged/minified away. Also check that the hosting build is serving the latest asset bundle and that no CDN/cache layer is delivering an older version without the focus styles. After deployment, validate with keyboard-only navigation in the production environment.

Another possibility is that the route matcher for match detail pages is too permissive and falls back to the home bracket view when the slug lookup fails, rather than triggering a 404.
1.error_message: Navigating to a non-existent match slug did not display a 404 page; the app returned or rendered the homepage instead.
1.recommended_fix_target: Configure the hosting/rewrite rules so only known application routes are rewritten to the SPA entry point and all other paths return a real 404. If this is a client-side routed app, add a proper catch-all 404 route in the frontend that checks for unknown match slugs and renders a not-found page instead of the homepage. Also verify the dynamic match page logic loads by slug and explicitly handles missing records with a 404 response/state.

1.recommended_fix_target: Update the sitemap to use a hostname that is publicly resolvable from external clients, or add/repair DNS records for worldcup2026.codercup.ai so it points to the deployed application. If the match pages are meant to live on the Amplify domain, regenerate the sitemap to emit canonical URLs on https://main.d2cyz5kp1vxns8.amplifyapp.com (or the correct custom domain) instead of the unreachable host. 2.name: Malformed match id renders a graceful error page
2.root_cause_hypothesis: The hosting layer is likely configured as a single-page app fallback that rewrites all unknown paths to index.html, so /match/!!! is being treated as a client-side route and served the homepage instead of a server-generated 4xx. This can happen when the reverse proxy/CDN rewrite rules are too broad, when no validation exists for match ID format on the server/edge, or when custom error pages are not configured and all routes default to the SPA entry point.
2.error_message: A graceful error page for a malformed match id was not rendered — the site shows the normal homepage instead of a 4xx-style error page.
2.recommended_fix_target: Update the hosting/router configuration so malformed dynamic routes like /match/!!! do not fall through to the SPA index. Add a dedicated 4xx/404 response for invalid match IDs, or configure route rewrites/redirects to only serve index.html for valid client-side routes and let invalid match paths return a real 404/4xx page. If using Amplify/CloudFront, adjust rewrite rules and custom error pages so '/match/<id>' is validated at the edge or by the app and invalid IDs render an error view instead of the homepage.

8.root_cause_hypothesis: The hosting side is likely serving a page shell that renders locale buttons client-side but does not include the SEO head metadata in the initial HTML response. This can happen if the app is deployed as a client-side SPA without SSR/SSG, if the head tags were not configured in the app build, or if an edge/CDN rewrite is returning an index.html template that lacks the <link rel="alternate" hreflang> entries. As a result, crawlers/tests inspecting the document head see no link elements even though the UI shows language options.
8.error_message: The page's <head> is missing the required hreflang alternate link entries for en, es, and pt.
8.recommended_fix_target: Add the missing hreflang alternate link tags in the server-rendered <head> for all locales (en, es, pt), e.g. <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="..." />, and make sure the hosting/deployment pipeline serves the fully rendered HTML rather than a client-only shell. If the site is built with a SPA framework, move SEO/head generation to SSR/SSG or use a head manager that injects links during server render. Also verify the locale URLs and canonical/alternate mappings are included in the deployed build and not removed by a CDN/edge transform or build optimization.

Because /api/match/this-does-not-exist/odds is not excluded from the fallback, the server returns the app HTML instead of an HTTP 404 JSON response from an API handler.
9.error_message: The unknown-match API did not return an HTTP 404 JSON response as expected. Instead, the SPA served HTML (index.html) for the API path.
9.recommended_fix_target: Update the hosting/rewrite configuration so that SPA fallback rules do not apply to /api/* routes. In Amplify/CloudFront this typically means adding an explicit route or function for /api/match/*/odds that returns a JSON 404 when the match is unknown, and only rewriting non-API browser routes to /index.html. If the API is meant to be served separately, place it behind a dedicated backend endpoint or API Gateway and ensure the frontend host proxies /api requests to that backend instead of the SPA.

9.name: Unknown API match returns 404 JSON with error and code
9.root_cause_hypothesis: The hosting layer is likely applying a single-page-app fallback rewrite that sends all unknown routes, including `/api/match/this-does-not-exist/odds`, to `index.html`. As a result the request never reaches an API handler that can generate a JSON 404 response, so the server returns HTML instead of the expected 404 JSON payload.
9.error_message: The API endpoint did not return the expected HTTP 404 JSON response containing 'error' and 'code'. Instead the SPA's index.html page (HTML) was served, preventing verification of a 404 JSON payload.
9.recommended_fix_target: Update the hosting/router configuration so `/api/*` requests are not rewritten to `index.html`. Exclude `/api/match/*/odds` from SPA fallback rules and ensure the API path is handled by the backend function/handler.
